title: Swadhyaya
one_line: The recital of Vedic verses and prayers in accordance with strict rules of recitation.
points: Swadhyaya is the recital of Vedic verses and prayers in accordance with strict rules of recitation.

Vedic hymns must be recited without damaging the artha (meaning) and Devata (deity) of a mantra through a wrong swara (pitch) or improper articulation of akshara (letter), pada (word), or varna (sentence).

The Gayatri mantra forms the basis for the study of all Vedic verses; mantras fall into Vedic (pragita and apragita) and Tantric (strilinga, pullinga, and napumsakalinga) categories, whose nature must be learned from a text called the Mantra Rahasya.
Guruji notes that such mantras are not very helpful to raja yoga and puts off discussing them.
Gods related to the mantras give siddhis (powers) to those who chant them and ponder their meanings.

sutra.translation: Owing to the learning and application of personal mantras, there is union with (one's) desired deity.
